title: Treasure map · Level 1: Four treasures, square legs
brief: Four treasures on the 100 mm grid, every leg from base along x or y (turns of 90 or 180 degrees; a treasure may lie on the way to another), then back to base. Line 1 of the program must be the one statement treasures = [(x, y), ...]: on a scored run the runner fills it in with that run's treasures; practice runs without it, so practise with seed 0's: treasures = [(1400, 300), (1100, 300), (1700, 300), (600, 300)]. A treasure is visited when the axle's middle passes within 50 mm of its centre. Base is the 200 x 200 mm square centred at (300, 300); the robot starts there facing +x, within 15 mm and 2 degrees. The level fixes the robot: the class robot (axle track 178 mm, as the program says) with an IMU on I2C 8. A run ends when the program ends, or at 90 s. Per run: 50 x treasures visited / 4, + 40 x min(1, 20 mm / end error) (the axle's middle to base's centre at the end), + 10 at or under par when all four are visited. Pass: a mean of at least 60 over 5 runs, and at least 4 runs that visit every treasure and end on base. Par: 25 s.

score.run: round(50 * visited / k + 40 * min(1, 20 / max(hypot(endX - baseX, endY - baseY), 0.001)) + if(visited == k & time <= par, 10, 0), 1)

complete.value: count(r in runs: r.visited == k & abs(r.endX - baseX) <= 100 & abs(r.endY - baseY) <= 100)
